newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Moslems clash in Nigeria, four reported dead.
newsitem.headline: Moslems clash in Nigeria, four reported dead.

text.p: Four people were killed on Friday in the northern Nigerian city of Kano when police opened fire on radical Moslems who were stoning them, residents of the city said.
A senior police officer reached by telephone from Lagos said he could only confirm the death of one person in the incident.
"I can confirm the death of one person. We are still gathering reports on the incident," he said.
Residents said trouble flared when members of the Shi'ite Moslem Brotherhood fundamentalist group tried to break up prayers at the city's central mosque to mark the end of the Ramadan fast.
"The police appealed to them to stop but in return they attacked the police with stones," said a lawyer from the city who was present.
"Police replied by firing at them and as they dispersed four of them fell to the ground and were later confirmed dead in hospital," he added.
The police officer said that two leaders of the Shi'ite group were arrested at the scene.
He said Kano was calm with armed police patrolling the city.
Religious clashes are common in the north where the majority of Nigeria's 50 million Moslems, about half the nation's population, live.

Majority of Nigerian Moslems are Sunni but there have been sporadic disturbances in the north involving the Shi'ite group, some of whose leaders have been detained over alleged incitement in their preaching.
Kano is one of the north's biggest cities with a population of about two million.
Last year five people were killed there in ethnic riots pitching the indigenous Hausa people against Ibo settlers from the eastern part of the country.
Kano was the focus of religious riots in the 1980s in the north in which thousands of people were killed.
